summary: Sort uses a fixed allowlist of SQL fragments, term and offset are parameterised or clamped; no release-blocking issue found.

Audit has 24 of 25 mandatory checks: the critical payment-verification check is missing, and the tests run only against local, so GO is not supported. Re-run the full audit including payment verification.

The /projects route trusts the client-supplied x-org-id header and never checks it against the user's orgIds, so any logged-in user can list another organisation's projects and budgets (IDOR). Validate membership server-side.
RLS is enabled with owner-scoped policies for all operations, anon is revoked, and the update relies on RLS correctly; no release-blocking issue found.

All mandatory checks pass with runtime evidence at the audited commit; the one finding (no per-account login rate limit, medium) has a named owner, approver, reason, edge IP rate limiting as mitigation and a fix date. Release with that risk tracked.

The internal DELETE route only calls requireSession and sits outside the admin middleware matcher, so any authenticated member can permanently delete any user account. Require an admin role check in the handler.
Webhook verifies the signature, only acts on paid sessions, and dedupes the event atomically in the same transaction as the plan update; no release-blocking issue found.

Checkout offers delayed-payment methods (bacs_debit, customer_balance), but the webhook upgrades the plan on checkout.session.completed without checking payment_status, so users get Pro before paying. The event is also recorded before processing, so a failed update is never retried.

The startsWith allowlist check can be bypassed (e.g. images.partner-cdn.com.evil.com), and fetch follows redirects, giving SSRF to internal hosts. There is also no size or content-type validation on the stored image.

Audit records an accepted high-severity finding: password reset tokens never expire (a two-day-old token was accepted), which is an account takeover risk. A 'low volume' justification is not adequate to ship it, so fix it first.
The critical ownership check was executed against the older commit 8393bb6, not the audited release commit ab2eaab, so the evidence is stale. Re-run it at the release commit before any GO.

document_preview is SECURITY DEFINER, granted to authenticated and filters only by id, so it bypasses RLS and any signed-in user can read the title and first 280 characters of any document. Use security invoker or filter by auth.uid().
All 25 mandatory checks pass with runtime evidence at the release commit, with no findings or accepted risks; the audit commit only adds the audit file.

The transfer view does not reject negative or zero amounts, so a user can send a negative amount and pull money from any recipient. Invalid amounts or unknown recipients also raise unhandled 500s; validate amount > 0 and handle errors.

The critical tenant-isolation check is backed only by static reading, with no command or runtime evidence, and src/routes.py contains no organisation filter at all. Critical checks need runtime evidence, so this cannot be GO.

The invoice route uses a session-scoped client, so the findFirst query is correctly limited to the caller's userId and returns 404 otherwise. Note the scoped client does not cover other operations such as findUnique or update, so route authors should be careful there.

The line object spreads the client-supplied input after unitAmount, so a caller can send their own unitAmount or name and set the price. Build lines from server-side product data only and validate quantity as an integer.
